photos.question: A client takes high-dose aspirin daily for arthritis and now reports ringing in the ears. What should the nurse suspect?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #350!

👂 Ringing ears on a daily pain reliever? Know this warning sign!

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Salicylate (aspirin) toxicity

🧠 Rationale: Tinnitus is a classic early sign of salicylate toxicity.

Hold the dose and report it to the provider.

Other signs include nausea, fast breathing and confusion.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Aspirin (Salicylates)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 NSAID, salicylate, antiplatelet

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Pain, fever, inflammation

🔹 Low dose to prevent heart attack and stroke

⚠️ Toxicity Signs:

🔹 Tinnitus or hearing loss

🔹 Nausea, vomiting

🔹 Rapid breathing, confusion

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Hold the dose and notify the provider

✅ Teach to take with food

✅ Watch for GI bleeding

✅ Avoid in children with viral illness (Reye syndrome)

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Aspirin overload rings the alarm: tinnitus = toxicity!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client is going home with a 24-hour Holter monitor. Which instruction should the nurse give?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #351!

❤️ Going home with a heart monitor? What is the client's job?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Keep a diary of activities and symptoms

🧠 Rationale: A Holter monitor records the heart rhythm for 24 to 48 hours.

The diary lets the provider match symptoms to the rhythm.

The client should do normal daily activities and keep the device dry.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Holter Monitor

❤️ Purpose:

🔹 Records continuous ECG at home

🔹 Finds rhythm problems that come and go

📝 Patient Teaching:

✅ Write down activities, symptoms and times

✅ Keep up normal daily activities

✅ Do not shower or swim while wearing it

✅ Keep electrodes on the skin

⚠️ Report Right Away:

🔹 Chest pain, fainting or severe dizziness

🔹 Call 911 for emergencies, do not wait for results

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Holter = Hold on and write it down. Live normally, log every symptom!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #HolterMonitor #ECG #Dysrhythmias #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: One day after abdominal surgery, a client has diminished breath sounds at the lung bases and a low-grade fever. Which action should the nurse encourage?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #352!

🫁 Day 1 after surgery, quiet lung bases and a low fever. What helps most?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Cough, deep breathe and use the spirometer

🧠 Rationale: These findings point to atelectasis, collapsed alveoli.

Coughing, deep breathing and the incentive spirometer reopen the alveoli.

Good pain control helps the client breathe deeply.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Postoperative Atelectasis

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Diminished breath sounds at the bases

🔹 Low-grade fever in the first day or two

🔹 Low SpO2, shortness of breath

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Incentive spirometer 10 times every hour while awake

✅ Turn, cough and deep breathe

✅ Get the client up and walking early

✅ Splint the incision with a pillow

✅ Give pain medication as ordered

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 SpO2 keeps dropping

🔹 Fever rises or sputum changes

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Atelectasis after surgery? Breathe deep, cough strong, walk long!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Respiratory #Atelectasis #PostOp #IncentiveSpirometer #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client with Graves disease has bulging eyes (exophthalmos). Which instruction should the nurse give?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #353!

👁️ Bulging eyes from an overactive thyroid. How do you protect them?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Use eye drops and raise the head of the bed

🧠 Rationale: Exophthalmos can keep the eyelids from closing fully.

Artificial tears keep the cornea moist.

Raising the head of the bed reduces swelling around the eyes.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Exophthalmos (Graves Disease)

⚠️ Signs of Graves Disease:

🔹 Bulging eyes

🔹 Weight loss, heat intolerance

🔹 Fast heart rate, tremor

🚨 Eye Care Teaching:

✅ Use artificial tears often

✅ Raise the head of the bed at night

✅ Wear dark glasses outside

✅ Tape eyelids closed at night if ordered

✅ Limit salt to reduce swelling

🚑 Report Right Away:

🔹 Eye pain or vision changes

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Graves eyes: Moisten, Elevate, Shield!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which milestone should the nurse expect in a healthy 12-month-old?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #354!

👶 First birthday! Which skill should this baby have?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Pulls to stand and cruises furniture

🧠 Rationale: Most 12-month-olds pull to stand and walk while holding furniture.

Many take first steps alone around this age.

Running and kicking a ball come closer to age 2, and a tricycle around age 3.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: 12-Month Milestones

🧸 Motor Skills:

🔹 Pulls to stand, cruises furniture

🔹 May take first steps alone

🔹 Pincer grasp to pick up small things

🗣️ Language + Social:

🔹 Says mama or dada and 1 to 2 words

🔹 Waves bye-bye

🔹 Plays simple games like peekaboo

📏 Growth:

🔹 Birth weight about triples by 1 year

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Refer if the child cannot stand with support

✅ Refer if the child loses skills

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

At 1 year: Stand, cruise, wave and say a word!

photos.question: A client at 30 weeks of pregnancy receives terbutaline for preterm labor. Which side effect should the nurse watch for?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #355!

🤰 A drug to slow early labor. Which side effect do you watch for?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Fast heart rate (tachycardia)

🧠 Rationale: Terbutaline is a beta-2 agonist that relaxes the uterus.

It stimulates the heart and causes tachycardia and tremors.

Hold it and notify the provider if the maternal heart rate is over 120/min.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Terbutaline (Tocolytic)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Beta-2 adrenergic agonist

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Short-term delay of preterm labor

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Maternal and fetal tachycardia

🔹 Tremors, nervousness

🔹 High blood glucose, low potassium

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check maternal HR before each dose

✅ Monitor fetal heart rate

✅ Report chest pain or shortness of breath

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Terbutaline = Tachycardia. Both start with T!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #OBNursing #PretermLabor #Terbutaline #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client on the mental health unit says, "I don't want to talk right now." Which response by the nurse is best?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #356!

🧠 The client does not want to talk. What should the nurse say?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — I will sit here with you for a while.

🧠 Rationale: Offering self shows caring and respect without pushing.

"Why" questions can make a client defensive.

Giving advice or leaving for a full day blocks trust.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Therapeutic Communication

✅ Therapeutic Techniques:

🔹 Offering self

🔹 Silence

🔹 Open-ended questions

🔹 Reflecting feelings

⚠️ Nontherapeutic Blocks:

🔹 Asking why

🔹 Giving advice or false reassurance

🔹 Changing the subject

🔹 Leaving the client alone for long periods

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Respect the client's pace

✅ Stay calm and present

✅ Check back often

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

When they won't talk, don't walk. Offer yourself!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!
